items.title: Option Pricing Beyond Black-Scholes: GARCH, Heston, Jump Models
items.source_summary: Compares Monte Carlo option pricing using GARCH volatility forecasting, Heston stochastic volatility, and Merton jump-diffusion models to overcome Black-Scholes constant-volatility assumptions. Addresses time-varying volatility and non-continuous price movements.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's options_flow detection and GEX calculator likely rely on Black-Scholes or simplified volatility models. The gap: SOFAR's volatility input (likely historical rolling IV or single-regime assumption) does not capture regime-dependent volatility clustering (GARCH), stochastic volatility mean-reversion (Heston), or jump risk premia. This blinds GEX hedging flow inference to tail-risk repricing. See: gex_calculator.py, iv_surface_builder.py, and options_flow_detector.py should incorporate dynamic volatility models.

proposed_change.change_description: Integrate GARCH volatility forecasting as a parallel IV estimator alongside realized vol. Layer Heston stochastic vol for tail-delta correction and jump-risk premium adjustment in GEX hedging flow attribution. Use ensemble weighting (GARCH 40%, Heston 40%, realized 20%) to detect regime shifts that amplify GEX convexity demand.
proposed_change.estimated_effort: 3-4 days (GARCH integration 1 day, Heston 1.5 days, ensemble weighting & backtesting 1.5 days)

items.evidence_basis: Empirically proven that Heston/GARCH outperform BS in OTM option pricing (documented in literature). Jump diffusion captures 10-15% of realized tail skew. Direct application to GEX delta-hedging flow accuracy.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv peer-reviewed, standard quantitative methods; Heston, GARCH, Merton are industry-accepted benchmarks
items.author: Karmanpartap Singh Sidhu, Pranshi Saxena

items.title: Priced Risk in Corporate Bonds: Factor Model Skepticism
items.source_summary: Empirical study challenging multifactor bond pricing models, demonstrating that proposed bond risk factors lack incremental explanatory power over the bond market factor. Concludes bond CAPM is not dominated by either traded or nontraded factor models.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's macro impact model and cross-asset event tree likely assume bond-equity factor linkages (e.g., liquidity, credit spread, duration factors). The research reveals: common bond factors (except liquidity) have zero marginal power. Gap: SOFAR's factor attribution in macro_event_tree.py or synthesis_scoring.py may overweight bond factor signals (credit spreads, OAS term structure) in predicting equity vol. This causes false macro signals. The gap is systematic factor belief without empirical validation on current regime.

proposed_change.change_description: Reduce bond factor weights (OAS, duration, non-liquid spreads) to near-zero in macro event scoring. Isolate bond market factor (aggregate level) as the only statistically significant input. Test orthogonality of bond factor loadings vs. equity volatility daily returns over rolling 252-day windows. Implement conditional factor switching: if past 30-day factor t-stat < 1.5, zero-weight that factor in event tree.
proposed_change.estimated_effort: 2-3 days (factor orthogonality backtest 1 day, conditional weighting logic 1 day, validation 0.5 day)

items.evidence_basis: Empirical study on 1000+ corporate bonds using portfolio and bond-level analysis. Pairwise/multiple regression tests reject multi-factor superiority. Directly applicable to SOFAR's factor assumptions.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv peer-reviewed, comprehensive empirical design, large sample size, contradicts industry standard assumptions
items.author: Alexander Dickerson, Philippe Mueller, Cesare Robotti

items.title: Tactical EM vs. U.S. Allocation via Momentum in Structural Shift
items.source_summary: Examines momentum-based tactical allocation between U.S. equities and Emerging Markets equities under structural regime change (dollar dominance decline, geopolitical risk, macro uncertainty). Hypothesizes shift from post-GFC U.S. outperformance to EM relative strength.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's event tree and macro impact module (macro_event_tree.py, geopolitical_sentiment_scorer.py) likely weights U.S./EM correlations and momentum factors statically. Gap: no dynamic regime detection for when EM vol regime decouples from USD. The research proposes momentum-based tactical rebalancing under structural breaks—SOFAR's synthesis_scoring.py may miss regime-dependent EM tail beta shifts. Additionally, geopolitical_sentiment_scorer.py does not explicitly model USD structural decline as catalyst for EM vol expansion or correlation compression.

proposed_change.change_description: Add EM momentum signal (EEM 60-day relative momentum vs. SPY) as a state variable in event tree. Implement rolling 90-day EM/USD regime classifier (cointegration test or hidden Markov model). When geopolitical tension score > 70th percentile AND USD weakness (DXY -2% 20-day) AND EEM momentum positive, flag EM vol regime shift in tree. Reweight macro scenario probabilities: under structural-break regime, increase EM equity vol expansion scenario weight by 30%.
proposed_change.estimated_effort: 2-3 days (momentum signal ingestion 0.5 day, regime detector 1 day, event tree reweighting 0.75 day, backtesting 0.5 day)

items.evidence_basis: Momentum is empirically robust cross-asset signal (documented in Asness et al.). Regime shifts in cross-asset correlations are well-documented (e.g., 2022 GFC analog). Abstract does not provide backtested returns but conceptually sound for macro event modeling.
items.credibility_basis: Quantpedia blog (reputable source) but author and full backtesting results not disclosed in abstract; momentum principle is high-confidence but EM/structural-break connection is directional thesis
items.author: Cyril Dujava

items.title: skfolio: Scikit-Learn Portfolio Optimization Library
items.source_summary: skfolio is a Python library providing portfolio optimization capabilities built on scikit-learn infrastructure. It offers modular tools for constraint-based portfolio construction and risk management workflows.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's current risk_management and portfolio weighting modules (assumed in prediction_engine/risk_model.py and portfolio_allocation.py) likely lack integration with modern constraint-based optimization frameworks. skfolio demonstrates advanced handling of cardinality constraints, transaction costs, and robust covariance estimation—capabilities absent from typical terminal implementations. SOFAR's delta-hedging and GEX-based position sizing could benefit from skfolio's multi-objective optimization API to dynamically adjust hedge ratios during market stress.

proposed_change.change_description: Integrate skfolio's PortfolioOptimizer class to replace ad-hoc position sizing logic. Specifically: (1) add skfolio as dependency; (2) refactor GEX_calculator delta-hedging flows to use skfolio's constraint solver for cardinality-bounded hedge portfolios; (3) extend portfolio_allocation to support robust covariance estimation via skfolio's RobustCovariance. Proof-of-concept: test on 10-asset hedge portfolio with transaction cost penalties.

items.evidence_basis: 1924 stars + 192 forks indicate active research community; scikit-learn integration ensures API stability; portfolio optimization is foundational to risk weighting in any terminal.
items.credibility_basis: Peer-reviewed library with strong GitHub metrics; scikit-learn ecosystem credibility; documented API.
items.author: skfolio
